İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanlığı'na yönelik ‘Yolsuzluk’ davasında, aralarında görevinden uzaklaştırılan Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun da bulunduğu 46’sı tutuklu 436 sanık, 109’uncu duruşmada hakim karşısına çıktı.
Duruşma savcısı, tüm tutuklu sanıkların tutukluluk halinin devamını talep etti. Duruşmaya 1 saat ara verildi.
Mahkeme, Mehmet Pehlivan, Fatoş Pınar Türker, Fatoş Ayık, Serhat Kapki, Ahmet Köksal, Onur Aldı, Volkan Ateş ve Murat Or'un tahliyesine karar verdi.
Medya A.Ş. Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Murat Ongun tahliye talebinde bulunurken, "Savunmamda da buraya çıktığım her anda da dedim ki, hala da diyorum bir kişi bile benim adımı rüşvete anmayacak. Neredeyse 500 kişi dinlediniz. Dedi mi bir kişi? En çok duyduğumuz şey ‘duydum, piyasadan duydum, sektörden duydum’. Bizim daha başta hukuki olarak tutuklanmamamız lazımdı. Sebep yokken sonuç icat ettiler, sonra da cezaevine attıkları insanlardan itirafçı yarattılar. Arz edilen hedef kişilerle ilgili suçlamalar yaptırdılar, başarılı da oldular. Büyük Türk milletinin bir ferdi olarak, bu millet gibi ben de cendereden çıkmayı Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’ten öğrendim. Belki zaman alır ama ben bu cendereden çıkarım. Vefatının da 88’inci yılında saygı ve minnetle anıyorum. Bu salonda bulunan, hukukun üstünlüğüne kalbiyle inanan, yaşam pratiğinde uygulayan herkese saygılarımı sunuyorum" dedi.
İBB Spor Kulübü Başkanı Fatih Keleş, “Soruşturma makamı beni İmamoğlu’nun kasası, bazı yerlerinde örgütün kasası, bazı yerlerinde ise beni en önemli kişi olarak tanımlıyor. Ben 149 eylemden cezalandırılması istenen ancak sıfatı belirsiz sözde bir örgüt yöneticisiyim. Tarafıma atfedilen suçlama ve soruşturma makamının beni oturttuğu konum dahi belirsizdir. Ne ana iddianamede ne de ek iddianamede kasa ya da en önemli kişi yakıştırmalarının hangi maddi delile dayandığı, sözde suç örgütünün hangi karar mekanizmasına dahil olduğum, yöneticilik vasfının ne suretle tecelli ettiği tek bir somut eylem ile açıklanabilmiş değildir. İddianame benim açımdan bol keseden dağıtılmış toplam bir ceza kampanyasıdır. Kimin kasasıyım? Hangi eylemlerim ile bu sıfatı hak ettim? Kime hangi talimatı verdim? Bunların hiçbiri yok. Ne bir görüntü kaydı, ne bir iletişim kaydı, ne bir bankacılık hareketi, ne bir fatura, ne bir sözleşme, ne bir mesaj kaydı, ne de tek bir yazılı kanıt. Bunların hiçbiri yok. Uydurma sözlerle tutuklandım. Gerçeğe aykırı bir kurguya imza atmadım, atmam. Etkin pişmanlık altında iftira mekanizması işletmedim, işletmem. Başkalarını haksız yere suçlamadım, suçlamam. Bugün karşınızda 20 aydır tutuklu bulunmamın en büyük sebebi bunları yapmayı reddettiğim içindir” dedi.
“ONLARCA İNSANIN GİZLİ TANIK BEYANLARIYLA TUTUKLANDIĞI ORTADADIR”
Ekrem İmamoğlu, "İddianame için kullandığım iftiraname sıfatı artık tescil edilmiştir. Gizli tanık üzerine kurulu bu paçavra yığını tarumar olmuştur. Onlarca insanın gizli tanık beyanlarıyla tutuklandığı ortadadır. Ancak o gizli tanıklar bugün ortada yoktur. İddia makamı iflas etmiştir. Elle tutulur tek bir tanık yoktur. Birkaç yandaş ve yalancı dışında şikayetçi kalmamıştır. Bu metin yalnızca beyan, dedikodu, duymuştum ifadeleriyle doldurulmuştur. Altına imza atanların terfi etmesiyle de bunun aslında bir terfiname olduğu tescil edilmiştir. Bu iddianame yargı tarihinin çöplüğünde en dibinde yerini bulmuştur. 602 gündür bu duvarların arkasındayım. Bu duvarlar bir insanın bedenini tutuyor olabilir ancak asıl tutsak edilen insanın bedeni değil, İstanbul’un, Türkiye ’nin, bu aziz milletin iradesidir. Onlar bir belediye başkanını tutukladıklarını sandılar. Oysa çok acı bir biçimde milletin iradesine kelepçe taktılar. Örgüt dediler, örgütü iddianame kurdu. Üyeler Silivri’de bir araya geldi. Burada tanıştık. Hayatımda hiç görmediğim örgüt yöneticim var benim. Kendi pislik içinde olan insanlar, bize çamur atmaya kalktılar. Fon vurgununu görüyorsunuz. Müştekilerimin hepsi geldi, dinledik. ‘Şikayetçi değilim’ dedi, gittiler" dedi.

Sarıgül ailesiyle başlayan kara para aklama soruşturmasında 17 kişi hakkında gözaltı kararı verildi.
Erzincan Milletvekili Mustafa Sarıgül’ün oğulları Emir ve Ömer Sarıgül’ün yanısıra eski eşi Aylin Kotil’in de tutuklandığı ‘kara para’ soruşturması başlatılmıştı.
Soruşturma kapsamında 17 gözaltı kararı verildi. 15 kişi gözaltı alındı.
Ahmet Tunç Akan, Sibel Aslanbaş, Arda Ali Can, Rıza Selim Demir, Hülya Turan, Meltem Ülgez, Elif Gülhan Eskiciooğlu, Gamze Kılınç Büyük, Alper Gündüz, Ramazan Elmas, Burak Çelebi, Mustafa Körpe, Yılmaz Güney, Remzi Onuk ve Emin Eres.
İstanbul başsavcılığının 16 Ekim’deki açıklamasına göre soruşturma, Alman vatandaşı K.P. ve M.B.’nin şikayetiyle başladı.
İddiaya göre iki isim, yurt içi ve dışında kurulan şirketler aracılığıyla kaynağı belirsiz yüksek miktarlı paraların aklandığını, Sarıgül ailesiyle ilgili bilgi ve belgeleri Murat Ağırel’e ilettiğini, fakat bunun ardından tehdit edildiğini söyledi.
Başsavcılık, Mustafa Sarıgül hakkındaki iddiaların da Ankara başsavcılığına gönderileceğini duyurdu.
YENİ Parti üyeliğinden 28 Ekim’de istifa eden Sarıgül hakkında cinsel istismar iddiaları da var.
Öte yandan gazeteci Timur Soykan, Murat Ağırel’le ilgili şöyle dedi: “Murat elindeki belgeleri yeterli bulmadığı için bir süre haberi beklemeye almıştı. Bir gazeteci sadece haber hazırlamak istediği için iftiralara maruz kalabiliyor. Maalesef bunu daha önce de yaşadık. Dostumuz Murat Ağırel’in suçsuzluğuna şahidiz.”
Ağırel’se ‘ilk kez yapmadığı bir haberden dolayı tutuklandığını’ yazdı.
Sarıgül’ün oğlu Emir Sarıgül’se savcılıkta verdiği 30 Ekim’deki ek ifadede şöyle söyledi:
“ Babam Mustafa Sarıgül tarafından Yeni Parti’ye verilmiş birtakım paralarla ilgili de bildiklerim vardır. Bunları da anlatmak istiyorum. Öncelikle Yeni Parti’nin kuruluş aşamasında, partinin genel merkez binasının iç tefrişatının yapılması için 250 bin dolar parayı Ankara’da Ümitköy’de bulunan bir restoranın çıkışında Özgür Özel’e ait aracın içerisine bıraktığını biliyorum.”
İstanbul başsavcılığı dün (9 Kasım) Mustafa Sarıgül’e hazırlanan tahkikat dosyasının yetkisizlik kararıyla Ankara başsavcılığına gönderildiğini duyurdu :
“28’inci dönem milletvekili Mustafa Sarıgül hakkında; suç örgütü kurma, çocuğun cinsel istismarı, suçtan kaynaklanan mal varlığı değerlerini aklama ve nitelikli cinsel saldırı suçlarından soruşturma yürütülmesi amacıyla hazırlanan tahkikat dosyası yetkisizlik kararı verilerek Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’na gönderilmiştir.”

Görevden uzaklaştırılan İBB Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu'nun da aralarında bulunduğu 46'sı tutuklu 436 sanığın yargılandığı İBB davasında ara karar açıklandı ve sekiz kişi hakkında tahliye kararı verildi.
İmamoğlu'nun avukatı Mehmet Pehlivan'ın dışında hakkında tahliye kararı verilen isimler şu şekilde:
Medya A.Ş.'de Genel Müdür ve Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Fatoş Pınar Türker, Medya A.Ş. Satın Alma ve İhale Müdürü Fatoş Ayık, Kültür A.Ş Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Onur Aldı, iş insanı Serhat Kapki, iş insanı Ahmet Köksal, kantar sorumlusu Volkan Ateş ve Ağaç A.Ş. çalışanı Murat Or.
Savcı, ara karar için mütalaasında tüm sanıkların tutukluluk halinin devamını talep etmişti.
Ekrem İmamoğlu 12 Kasım'daki duruşmada, "İlk defa bir nesil, kendinden önceki nesilden yoksul. Foncular dışında" dedi ve esnafın kepenk indirdiğini, sanayicinin çalışamadığını, bankacılığın iflas ettiğini belirtti.
İmamoğlu ayrıca gözaltına alındığı 19 Mart 2025'te ve CHP için mutlak butlan kararının verildiği 21 Mayıs 2026'da "en büyük kaybedenin Recep Tayyip Erdoğan olduğunu, kendisini hapse attırarak onu sandıkta yenemeyeceğini tüm dünyaya ilan ettiğini" söyledi.
İstanbul 33. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'nde görülen davanın üçüncü duruşması 2 Kasım'da başlamıştı.
12 Kasım Perşembe günkü duruşmada Ekrem İmamoğlu, Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek'in YENİ Parti Milletvekili Turan Taşkın Özer'i bütçe görüşmelerinde "tehdit ettiğini" belirtti ve "Dokunulmazlığın olmasa tutukluydun' dedi. Bu dert mahkemenin de derdidir" ifadelerini kullandı.
Ayrıca İmamoğlu, TİP Milletvekili Ahmet Şık'ın eşi Yonca Verdioğlu'nun gözaltına alınmasına, "Devlet esir alır mı?" şeklinde tepki gösterdi.
Ekrem İmamoğlu, eski İBB İştirakler ve Bağlı Kuruluşlar Komisyonu Başkanı Ertan Yıldız'a avukatlarının soru soramamasına da tepki gösterdi:
"Ertan Yıldız iddianamenin bel kemiğiydi, sorular soruldu, köşeye sıkıştı ve ne yazık ki benim avukatlarım ona tek bir soru bile soramadı, itirafçı duruşmadan götürüldü" dedi.
Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, henüz İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcısı iken "İBB soruşturmasının dönüm noktası Ertan Yıldız'ın itirafçı olması" diye konuşmuştu.
İmamoğlu, 21 gizli tanıktan yalnızca iki tanesinin duruşmaya geldiğini belirterek, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:
"Mahkeme başkanı bile dayanamadı gizli tanıklara. 'Alın götürün' dedi. Gizli tanıkla tutuklanan insanlar burada hâlâ. Bu dava çökmedi mi?" dedi ve sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:
"Benim tutuklanmama sebep olan gizli tanıklar Meşe, Çınar ve Doğan ortada yok."
Ekrem İmamoğlu ve mahkeme başkanı arasında yaşanan bir diyalog da kamuoyuna yansıdı.
İmamoğlu savunmasını sürdürürken mahkeme başkanı araya girdi, "Heyet olarak tavrınızdan memnun değiliz, el kol sallıyorsunuz" dedi.
Bunun üzerine Ekrem İmamoğlu, "12 metrekaredeyim ben, el kol ne ki? Ekrem'e ana avrat küfür ettiler" yanıtını verdi.
Mahkeme başkanı ise, "Bize de sosyal medyada neler neler söyleniyor" deyince İmamoğlu, "Biz şikayetçi oluyoruz, 'Kovuşturmaya yer yok' diyorlar. Siz şikayetçi olunca dava açarlar. Ben o konuda sizin de hakkınızı savunurum, yanınızda olurum" yanıtını verdi.
Mahkeme bu celsede dosyada "İlke", "Zeytin", "Martı" ve "Gürgen" kod adlı gizli tanıkların da üçüncü celse için duruşmada hazır edilmesini istemişti.
Yeni Parti lideri Özgür Özel, Aralık 2025'te "İlke" kod adlı gizli tanığın, verdiği ifadelerden kısa bir süre sonra tüm ifadelerini ve gizli tanıklık statüsünü resmen geri çektiğini beyan ettiğini aktarmıştı.
Soruşturmanın başlangıcında İmamoğlu'na yönelik beyanlarda bulunan ancak hazırlanan iddianamede yer almayan "Meşe" kod adlı gizli tanığın beyanlarının da iddianamede "İlke" kod adlı gizli tanığın beyanlarının arasında yer aldığı kaydedildi.
Gizli tanıklardan "Gürgen" ve "Zeytin" 4 Kasım tarihli duruşmada dinlendi. Diğer iki tanık duruşmada hazır edilmedi.
Gizli Tanık "Gürgen" rüşvet iddiaları ile ilgili mahkeme başkanının ve sanıkların sorularına "gördüğüm bir şey yok ama konuşulanlar böyledir" sözleriyle yanıt verdi.
Bilgilere nasıl ulaştığı sorusuna ise "bir yerden vakıf oldum" yanıtını verdi.
"Zeytin" ise imar ve ihale süreçleriyle ilgili suçlamalarıyla ilgili doğrudan bir tanıklığı olmadığını söyledi. İfadesinde adı geçen isimleri ise şahsen tanımadığını söyledi.
Avukatlar, hakkında iftira kapsamında suç duyurusunda bulunmasını talep etti.
Celsenin beşinci gününde, Beylikdüzü Belediye Başkanı iken tutuklanan Murat Çalık söz alarak tahliyesini talep etti.
9 Kasım'da konuşan Çalık, aleyhine olan herhangi bir delilin ortaya konulmadığını ve lehine olan ifadelerin arttığını belirtti. 20 aydır özgürlüğünden yoksun olduğunu söyleyen Çalık, delillerin büyük bölümünün toplandığını ve tutukluluğun devamını gerektirecek bir durum kalmadığını savundu.
Sağlık sorunlarına ilişkin sonuçların Adli Tıp Kurumu tarafından değiştirildiğini belirten Çalık, kâğıt üzerinde değiştirilen gerçeklerin insan bedeni üzerindeki gerçekleri değiştirmediğini söyledi.
Çalık, "Ben kimseden merhamet beklemiyorum sadece yaşam hakkımın korunmasını istiyorum" dedi.
Öte yandan tanık olarak dinlenen Tugay Düzgün ve Ali Kaan Yurt, itirafçı sanık Recep Taşçı'nın iddianame yayınlanınca kendilerini toplayıp "Baskı altındayım, 2 çocuğum var, böyle bir ifade vermek zorundaydım" dediğini söyledi.
Şişli Belediye Başkanı görevindeyken tutuklanan Resul Emrah Şahan da 9 Kasım'daki duruşmada söz alarak, Bu dosya müteahhitlerle iş takipçilerinin dedikodularına dayanıyor; ülkede vicdanı entübe edilenler var" dedi.
Kendisiyle ilgili birçok tanığın dinlendiğini ve hiçbirinin "Rüşvet aldı" demediğini ifade eden Şahan, 20 ayda dosyadaki delillerin çoktan toplandığını ifade etti:
"Vicdanınızla nereye varacağınızı söylemek bana düşmez ama oraya konuşmak zorundayım. Tahliyemi talep ediyorum."
Duruşmada, müşteki sıfatı ile dinlenen Mehmet İlhan Gülay, Avni Çelik ve Bahattin Uçar sanıklardan şikayetçi olmadıklarını belirtti.
Müşteki Çetin Gül, şikayetinin sürdüğünü ancak davaya müdahil olmak istemediğini söyledi.
Gül, tutuklu sanık Necati Özkan hakkında "Allah razı olsun, biz kendisinden memnunuz" ifadelerini kullandı.
Tanık olarak dinlenen Ahmet Taşçı, görgü tanığı olmadığını, ifadesinde anlattıklarının "duyuma dayalı" olduğunu söyledi.
Taşçı, mahkeme başkanının iddialarını neye dayandırdığı sorusuna "duyumlarım" cevabını verdi.
Taşçı'ya 19 Mart'ta belediyeye yönelik operasyonun ardından verdiği dilekçedeki "vicdanım rahat değil" ifadesi de soruldu.
Taşçı, "ben ceza vermişim gibi bir durum oluştu. Ben sadece bildiklerimi söyledim" dedi.
Tanıklardan Atlas Firması sahibi Ekrem Reşat Tüzün, İBB Başkan Danışmanı ve Medya AŞ Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Murat Ongun'un avukatı Rahşan Çetinkaya'nın "müvekkilim sizden usulsüz bir talepte bulundu mu" sorusuna "Hayır" cevabını verdi.
Etkin pişmanlık ifadesini geri çeken tutuklu sanık Murat Kapki, Tüzün'e "İhale almamda anormal bir durum var mı? Bir sürü şirket var, niye onları saymadın?" diye sordu.
Tüzün, "Duyumlarımdan bahsettim. Aklıma ilk gelen şirketleri söyledim" yanıtını verdi.
Tanıklardan Kameroğlu İnşaat çalışanı Aydın Şahin, iş insanı Adem Kameroğlu'nun yönlendirmesiyle bankadan çektiği 2 milyon TL'yi Necati Özkan'a teslim ettiğini iddia etti.
Özkan, bu suçlamaya yanıt olarak "Bu zaten bizim ifademiz. Dört dairenin bedeli olarak yatırılmıştır. Bana fiziksel olarak verilmedi. Kendileri çekip kendileri yatırdılar" dedi.
Tanık olarak dinlenen Abdi İbrahim şirketinin müdürü Cem Erdinç ise patronundan iskan problem ile ilgili talimat aldıklarını söyledi.
Erdinç, "yapılan görüşmeler neticesinde 3 milyon 500 bin dolar teslim edildiğini" iddia etti.
Şişli Belediye Başkanı Resul Emrah Şahan'ın avukatı Doğa Şanlıoğlu Erdinç'e müvekkiliyle görüşüp görüşmediğini sordu.

Özellikle Asya ülkeleri ve Avustralya'da kamu kuruluşları ile kilit öneme sahip sektörler kesintiden etkileniyor.
Türkiye'de de kullanıcılar bazı Microsoft programlarına erişemiyor.

Gorilla Technology adlı şirkette çalışan Spain, eposta ve Microsoft hizmetlerin kesilmesiyle şirketlerin bir iş günü kaybettiklerini ve ekonomik maliyetin milyonlarca dolara tırmanabileceğini söylüyor.

Öyle ki bu kritik operasyonun detayları şu şekilde: İstanbul İl Emniyet Müdürlüğü Siber Suçlarla Mücadele Şube Müdürlüğü ekiplerinin kurmuş oldukları 'Avcı' ismindeki bu sistem aslında siber devriyenin en kritik parçası olmuş durumda" ifadelerini kullandı.

Bu panel vasıtasıyla insanların kişisel bilgilerine erişme durumu içerisinde kalan şüphelilerin, bu erişimi sağlayabilmek adına ve aynı zamanda elde ettikleri bu bilgileri satmak vasıtasıyla kazandıkları paralar söz konusu. İşte tam da buna 'dur' diyor Avcı sistemi" sözleriyle şebekenin kirli çarkını deşifre etti.

Microsoft'un bulut tabanlı platformu Microsoft 365 ile Exchange Online altyapısına bağlı Outlook, Teams ve yapay zeka asistanı Copilot hizmetlerinde dün başlayan erişim sorunu, saatler boyunca devam etti. Kesinti, Asya-Pasifik bölgesinde bugünkü mesai saatlerine kadar uzandı.

Exchange Online altyapısına bağlı olmayan bazı özelliklerin ise kesinti boyunca çalışmaya devam ettiği bildirildi.

Sabah saatlerinden itibaren etkili olmaya başlayan kuvvetli rüzgar da hayatıı olumsuz etkilemeye başladı.
Eyüpsultan Yeşilpınar Mahallesi Girne Caddesi'ndeki 5 katlı binanın çatısından uçan parçalar, park halindeki 4 araca zarar verdi.

Sultangazi'de Cebeci ile Sultançiftliği mahallelerindeki bazı ağaçlar fırtına nedeniyle park halindeki araçların üzerine devrildi. Ekipler, devrilen ağaçlar ile hasar gören araçları kaldırmak için çalışma yaptı.

Şehir Hatları'ndan yapılan duyuruya göre, şiddetli rüzgar nedeniyle birçok sefer iptal edildi.
Maltepe-Adalar ile Beşiktaş-Adalar ve Kabataş Adalar seferleri ikinci bir duyuruya kadar yapılamayacak.
Ayrıca, Aşiyan-Anadolu Hisarı-Küçüksu Ring Hattı ve Aşiyan-Üsküdar Hattı seferleri ikinci bir duyuruya kadar Bebek-Küçüksu-Anadolu Hisarı-Bebek ve Bebek-Üsküdar olarak yapılacak.

Başta İstanbul, İzmir ve Bursa gibi şehirler olmak üzere birçok yerde hava sıcaklığı 22-23 dereceye kadar ulaştı. Kuvvetli lodos nedeniyle ulaşımda aksamalar ve ağaç devrilmesi gibi olumsuzluklar yaşandı .
Ancak bahar havası yerini kuvvetli sağanak ve yağmura bırakacak. İstanbul'da hava sıcaklığı 8 derece birden düşecek.
Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü tarafından yapılan son değerlendirmelere göre, bugün yurt genelinde parçalı ve yer yer çok bulutlu bir hava hakim olması bekleniyor.

Rüzgarın, genellikle güneyli yönlerden hafif, ara sıra orta kuvvette, Marmara ve Ege'de kuvvetli olarak eseceği tahmin ediliyor.

A NKARA Üniversitesi Eğitim Bilimleri Fakültesi öğretim üyesi Prof. Dr. Erten Gökçe, Ege Üniversitesi Eğitim Fakültesi öğretim üyesi Doç. Dr. Elif Ulu ve Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Eğitim Fakültesi öğretim üyesi Doç. Dr. Adem Doğan’a öğrencilerin ve ebeveynlerin ara tatili verimli geçirmek için neler yapması gerektiğini sorduk. İşte önerileri:
1- Çocuğunuza tatilde ne yapmak istediğini sorun. Birlikte bir plan hazırlayın. Ama her günü etkinlikle doldurmayın; dinlenmeye ve çocuğun kendi seçtiği şeylerle ilgilenmesine de zaman bırakın.
2- Uyku ve öğün düzenini gözetin. Tatilde saatler biraz değişebilir; yine de günlük düzenin okul günlerinden çok uzaklaşmamasına çalışın.
3- Her gün biraz hareket edin. Birliktey ürüyüşe çıkın, parkta oyun oynayın veya açık havada bol bol vakit geçirin.
4- Yeni bir spor deneyin. Çocuğun daha önce denemediği bir spor, belki de yeni bir uğraş edinmesinin ilk adımı olur.
5- Bisiklete binin. Ya da başka bir açık hava etkinliği seçin.
6- Ekran süresini birlikte planlayın. Telefon, tablet, bilgisayar ve televizyon kullanımına ilişkin anlaşılır sınırlar koyun.
7- Birlikte kitap seçin. Okuma zamanını keyifli bir etkinlik olarak planlayın.
8- Sesli okuma zamanları oluşturun. Okumayı yeni öğrenen çocuklarla her gün kısa süre sesli okuma yapın.
9- Tabelalar, etiketler oyununuz olsun. Tabelaları, ürün ambalajlarını, kitap başlıklarını veya kısa notları birlikte okuyun. Çocuğunuzun doğru okuyup okumadığını sınamak yerine kelimeler üzerine sohbet edin.
10- Hikâyeleri birlikte okuyun. Çocuğunuzdan hikâyeye kendi sonunu eklemesini isteyin.
11- Matematiği günlük yaşama taşıyın. Yemek hazırlarken malzemeleri sayın, tarifteki ölçüleri karşılaştırın veya alışverişte fiyatlara bakın.
12- Bir yere giderken yolculuğun ne kadar süreceğini tahmin edin, uzaklığı ölçün. Çocuğunuzdan saatleri, mesafeleri ve geçen süreyi bulmasını isteyin.
13- Kutu oyunları oynayın. Puan toplama, zar atma veya hamle sırası bekleme gibi kuralları olan oyunlar seçin.

Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.
Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

Many prominent voices in technology and the president of the US have publicly supported the former Nvidia CEO despite his ouster.
Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with a direct report. The situation surrounding Huang has unfolded quickly, with The New York Times only reporting on Friday that Huang and the suspected spy were “close” before other dominoes started to fall, leading to a swift fall from grace for one of the biggest names in technology. (Hours after Huang’s resignation was announced, Reuters reported that he also had an “intimate relationship” with another Nvidia employee.)
Prominent voices in technology have come out in support of Huang, with some calling the resignation a “waste” and a sad day for “all humanity.” The narrative among those leaders on X, at least, is that Huang’s resignation was rushed — perhaps an overreaction to salacious news stories about his personal life. Some others have had a more neutral reaction, commenting more on Huang’s achievements at the company’s helm. You can see a collection of those responses below.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”, Trump said on Truth Social .
Elon Musk said in a reply to an X user that it would “be an honor” to hire Huang. He also replied to a post that said “You’d think we’d have learned from Steve Jobs and Travis Kalanick that one does not just simply replace the founder…” by saying “True words.”
Sweeney said that today is “A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction.”
Ahead of Huang’s resignation, Sweeney posted about how Huang “saved” a GDC 2015 presentation by dropping off a graphics card and said that “The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said last night, before Huang’s resignation was announced.
Mullenweg reposted an X post that followed his brief September ouster as CEO : “Founder advice: If you don’t have a coup attempt every few years, you’re not hiring strong enough leaders.” He said , “Just putting this back out there, for no reason whatsoever.”
“What a waste,” Hansson said this morning , replying to his own post from hours before : “NVIDIA would be wrong to fire Jensen. His marital indiscretions are between him, his wife, and a reprimand from the board. Have some proportionality.”
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened,” Delangue said . “It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!
“It’s a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign,” Zhao said .
“If that Spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal,” Steinberger said . “Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.” (“I agree,” replied Sweeney .)
Srinivas thanked Huang for “33 years of bold leadership” in a post this morning . “You built a small startup into America’s most valuable company, with relentless improvement. The tech company said it is attempting to improve capacity to enable more users to get back on its systems, after a global outage affected millions of users for more than 12 hours on Thursday and Friday.

The issue appears patchy, with some but not all users reporting problems with services including Microsoft Teams and Outlook email. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Copilot, Microsoft’s AI chatbot, according to the company.
Microsoft said that there were no indications that the outage was caused by a cyber-attack.
Earlier, the company had said it was only seeing “marginal success” from its efforts to bring its systems fully back online. It had said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” – which was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”.
The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” because of a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.
It earlier warned that services that have restarted can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic.
“Once mitigated, we will provide full details of the root cause, defense-in-depth repair items, and more within a post-incident report,” Microsoft said.
The outage website Down Detector showed an increase in Microsoft 365 problems at about 1pm ET, with nearly 130,000 reports of problems in 74 countries affecting access to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams as well as enterprise services such as SharePoint and OneDrive. AI assistant Copilot was also affected.

OpenAI said it was investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors in which new connections may be broken and tools were not working as ⁠expected. Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider ​affecting its Microsoft 365 ​connector.
Microsoft last month reported an ​outage of its Azure cloud platform that affected a ​suite of productivity software ‌and a range ​of industries worldwide.
Mark Gregory, an associate professor in the School of Engineering at RMIT University, said the outage appears to be affecting the network layer in Microsoft’s systems, and was potentially similar to the configuration issue that brought down Optus’s network in 2023 .
He said when some of the servers have configuration issues, it means customers are forced to share a smaller pool of servers to access the cloud services.
“If you lose part of that pool, then all of the users are trying to access the remaining servers, and that overloads them. And then they go down.
“And so you end up with a cascading problem. Then it takes time to find the underlying problem, in this case, a misconfiguration in the network layer.”
Gregory said it showed companies should invest more in testing environments for configuration changes before deployment in the live network, and said businesses reliant on cloud services such as Microsoft 365 should have backup options.

In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

US House Speaker Mike Johnson has said ⁠there is a ​growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .
Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US ⁠authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government. The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.
In the last week, representatives from both sides of the aisle have called for tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips; chips that could underpin China’s surging AI development.
Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are ⁠widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US ​has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips ‌because it wants its own companies to stay ahead in the race.
“The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here,” Johnson told ‌reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China’s access to the advanced technology. “I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.“
Congressional Republicans are keen to attach ​new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defense authorisation bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke to Reuters on the condition of anonymity.
This live blog is now closed – but if you’d like to read more on Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia, our latest report is here .
Colette Kress – Nvidia’s interim CEO – was one of the few executives at the company willing to check Jensen Huang’s enormous, often risky ambitions, Reuters has reported, citing two sources familiar with the matter.
Kress ⁠and her staff clashed with Huang and the company’s sales team over the massive financing deals that fed into what some Wall Street critics deemed a circular AI economy, including investments in OpenAI ​and AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda, according to one of the people familiar with ‌the matter.
A proposed $250bn plan to support an OpenAI ‌data center project in Ohio was ultimately pared to $120bn.
“I think it’s unlikely anyone but Jensen is going to invest in his own customers as aggressively,” said a third source, a venture capital investor. ‌
Kress served as an important counterweight to Huang, whose ⁠success afforded him great latitude on key decisions, the sources said.
“Colette is a pragmatist,” a fourth source told Reuters. She can project calm and help stabilize markets while the search is ongoing, the person said, adding that Kress had been on recent calls to reassure customers and suppliers as the tumult inside the company unfolded.
Under her leadership, Nvidia is likely to “approach DC more like other tech companies do, by trying to build capital and make friends,” instead of picking “a fight over export controls” the way it did under Huang’s leadership, ‌the person said.
Jensen Huang had enjoyed rock-star status in China, where his visits drew crowds seeking selfies and autographs, with his casual outings became social-media sensations. During a January 2026 visit, opportunistic sellers advertised photographs with the former Nvidia chief for 25,000 yuan, while a Beijing restaurant launched a special menu costing more than 400 yuan after he ate there.
On Chinese social media, many expressed surprise at what they saw as the swift resignation of the former Nvidia CEO, and mourned the sudden end of his three decades at the top of the company.
News of his resignation attracted more than 400m views overnight on Chinese microblogging platform Weibo.

Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.
Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.
The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.
Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.
Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.
The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.
Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.
Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.
Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."
The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.
"The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.
Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.
Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.
Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace.
He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.
Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.
Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".

China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, the Guardian understands.
The decision will disappoint many countries and climate experts, who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the lead on the global stage, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate .
Al Gore, the former US vice-president, was among those left disheartened by the decision. “I would be very much in favour of that idea [of China hosting the summit],” he told the Guardian. “It’s too bad.”
China is in the midst of an economic transformation , from being heavily dependent on coal to becoming an “electro state”. John Kerry, the former US secretary of state, told the Guardian that China was leaving the rest of the world behind in forging and using the low-carbon technologies of the future.
Renewable energy generation capacity has now outstripped coal in China, and its greenhouse gas emissions appear to have declined slightly this year.
Sales of electric vehicles in the country have also taken off, making up nearly two-thirds of the market last month, and China’s clean energy industries drove more than 90% of the country’s investment growth last year .
The rules of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) mean an Asian country should host in 2028.
Gareth Redmond-King, the international lead at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit thinktank, said China’s position as an industrial powerhouse would have made it a formidable contender to hold the summit.
“It would undoubtedly be significant for the world’s biggest emitter and second-biggest economy to host a climate Cop,” he said.
“They’re leading the world on investment, manufacture and deployment of clean energy tech, and their emissions have started to tick down. As a leadership story, China hosting Cop33 would be a big deal.”
It is not clear why China has decided against hosting the conference, but several experts that spoke to the Guardian suggested that the US electoral cycle was likely to have been a factor. The next US presidential election will take place on 7 November 2028, and Cop33 is scheduled for 6 to 17 November that year.
After the strong showing by Democrats in the recent midterm elections, in which voter concern over the climate crisis was thought to be a factor , the Democrats will be hoping to elect a climate-friendly president in 2028. But even if they succeed, Trump will still be in office until the following January.
The US president rejects climate science and withdrew the US from the Paris agreement, and is also withdrawing from its parent treaty, the 1992 UNFCCC.
China seeks to be seen as a leader among developing countries, but has been wary of stepping into the gap left by the US. Under the Democratic presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, the US and China enjoyed a close partnership on climate issues , setting joint targets on reducing methane and developing clean technology.
Cop33 will be an important meeting because it will include the “global stocktake” – a mechanism under the 2015 Paris climate agreement that examines countries’ progress on cutting emissions in line with the goal of limiting global temperature rises to 1.5C.
That limit is now certain to be surpassed, but experts say countries should now try to minimise the temperature “ overshoot ”, to avoid worse ravages from extreme weather.
India’s government considered offering to host Cop33 for several months earlier this year, but also decided against it. India’s coal use has been increasing, even as the country exceeds its own renewable energy targets.
The Guardian understands that other countries mulling a bid to host Cop33 include Uzbekistan, South Korea, Indonesia and Thailand.
No decision on a host is likely to be made at this year’s Cop31 meeting , which is ongoing in Turkey, with the Turkish and Australian governments jointly presiding over the summit.

Van Hollen is the son of former US diplomats known for his antiwar position and for championing progressive causes.
United States Senator Chris Van Hollen has declared that he is running for Senate majority leader as Democrats prepare to take charge of the US Congress in January, following a Democratic landslide in this month’s midterm elections.
Van Hollen said in a post on X late on Thursday that Americans had “called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption”.
“To deliver, we need new leadership,” he wrote, adding that “this isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call.
He is a Democratic senator from Maryland who has been in Congress since 2003, rising to prominence for his opposition during the second term of US President Donald Trump.
Van Hollen was born in 1959 in Karachi, Pakistan. His father was a Foreign Service officer who later served as the US deputy assistant secretary of state for Near Eastern and South Asian affairs.
His mother worked at the CIA and the US Department of State.
Van Hollen has had mounting calls to enter the race for Senate majority leader amid growing opposition to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s continued tenure, over criticism of his handling of the Democratic caucus during the Trump presidency.
US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed from Michigan has said he will not support Schumer as the majority leader in the Senate and welcomed Van Hollen’s decision to run.
In a post on X, El-Sayed said: “I called on Sen. Chris Van Hollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience.
“We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority,” El-Sayed said.
In April 2025, Van Hollen drew attention when he travelled to El Salvador to meet a Maryland resident mistakenly deported by the Trump administration, in a case which ultimately saw Kilmar Abrego Garcia returned to the US.
In September, Van Hollen forced a vote on a resolution that would have required the Trump administration to report on the killing of nine Americans in the occupied West Bank and on Israel’s treatment of Palestinian children in military detention. The resolution failed 47-53, with senators voting largely along party lines.
In August 2025, Van Hollen accompanied US Senator Jeff Merkley to the Rafah crossing at Egypt’s border with Gaza as Israel continued to prevent humanitarian aid delivery to Palestinians in the enclave.
Van Hollen has repeatedly challenged Washington’s relationship with Israel and has called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “ chronic liar “. He told Al Jazeera earlier this year that the US-Israel war on Iran “is making America and our allies less safe”.
Van Hollen has been one of the foremost advocates for ending Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and violations in the occupied West Bank.
He has consistently pushed for strict accountability for Israeli actions and for restricting US military assistance to Israel.

Reports of alleged incident follow US envoys’ meetings with the Russian and Ukrainian president.
Finland’s military says its forces have detected a rare strike on a Russian navy vessel in the Baltic Sea as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised mediation efforts led by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
A spokesperson for the Nordic country’s military said in an email to the Reuters news agency that its forces “detected … a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation”, adding that Finland is not under “any immediate military threat”.
The statement did not provide further details on where the strike originated, the location or timing of the incident, or how it was detected.
Reuters said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties or what had caused Wednesday’s strike.
Estonia shares a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea with Finland. Local media reported that the vessel was a small Russian navy ship which had returned to Saint Petersburg after the alleged attack.
Ukraine’s Security Service has said it carried out the attack, according to Finnish broadcaster Yle. In recent days, Russia said it had intercepted at least 146 Ukrainian drones in the northwestern Leningrad region.
On Wednesday, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania had issued warnings to citizens to take shelter due to drones in their airspace, and NATO warplanes were scrambled in response.
On Thursday, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow before meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland.
The US shuttle diplomacy followed trilateral negotiations in the United Arab Emirates this week, which produced no major breakthrough, aside from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners .
Russia’s state-run news agency TASS reported that the prisoner exchange should happen in two to three weeks. If finalised, it would be the latest in a long line of such exchanges.
“We are also working toward what would be the largest prisoner exchange of the war, potentially reuniting thousands of people with their families,” Kushner said on X on Thursday, following his meetings.

A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.
European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.
When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.
The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi , followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy .
Zelenskyy and Kushner also said Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.
Kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine , alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.
"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.
But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.
Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.
"Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations."
Europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.
"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.
European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.
Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that."

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.
Putin said a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove new joiners Finland and Sweden , could be among his demands.
"What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately."
This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of , especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.
"Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," said Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?"
US President Donald Trump said publicly that he was hoping for a "very big, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe."
Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.
They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most important: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.
The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.
Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.
Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.
But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.

A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October.
The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m. on October 24.
The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date.
Under the government's proposal, the license fee model that currently funds Czech Television (CT) and Czech Radio (CRo) would be scrapped, and the broadcasters would be funded directly from the state budget.
The three parties in the coalition — Babis's centrist ANO, the far-right SPD, and radical conservative Motorists, whose voter bases tend to be less affluent — insist that the license fee is an unfair tax.
The parties argue that the new arrangement, which would see funding for CT and CRo cut by around 15% in the first year, would make the two more efficient. They also point out that several other European Union states have made similar changes.
Opposition parties, civil society organizations and international watchdogs accuse the government of seeking to undermine the independence of the broadcasters, whose critical reporting has long irked ANO and the SPD in particular.
Analysts point out that while models in other EU states include guarantees of long-term financial stability and editorial independence, the Czech government proposal offers neither.
CT and CRo have warned that the reduced budget included in the bill will mean programming- and staff cuts .
When the first publication of the proposed bill was met with protests over the summer, Vaclav Stetka of the European New School of Digital Studies told DW that such "dramatic budget cuts represent an act of cultural vandalism."
There has also been condemnation of the restriction of the parliamentary debate amid the fast-tracking of the bill.
"The confrontational approach, the attempts to limit parliamentary debate and the government's rhetoric towards journalists and critics have all contributed to the public backlash," Otto Eibl, political scientist at Masaryk University in Czechia 's second city Brno, told DW.
The backlash was immediate. Crowds picketed parliament through the night as the government pushed through the first reading of the bill.
Since then, multiple rallies have taken place in cities and towns across the country. Many of these protests were led by students and joined by unions, Churches and representatives of educational and cultural institutions.
CT and CRo staff called a strike in early November, disrupting the country's TV and radio schedules.
It will take place two days before the anniversary of the start of the Velvet Revolution, which ultimately brought down communism in what was then Czechoslovakia in 1989.
The civil society group Million Moments for Democracy, which is organizing Sunday's rally, brought an estimated 300,000 onto the streets to protest during Babis's first term as prime minister in 2019 and more than 200,000 earlier this year .
The government's sudden bid to push through the proposal reflects impatience to deliver on a core pledge made ahead of the October 2025 election, as well as the longstanding ambition of the prime minister, who was stymied in his attempt to engineer control of CT's governing council during his first term in power in 2017–21.
Vaclav Stetka notes that repeated assaults on public media by Czech governments past and present reflect a particular political culture across Europe's post-communist states.
"The political elite has never accepted the independence of public media," he asserted.
In Czechia, however, the public broadcasters have earned special status as cornerstones of democracy .
That standing was forged in what became known as the "Czech TV crisis" of 2000–01, when an occupation of CT's studios by staff and mass protests forced the government of the day to back down on a bid to wrest control.
"The fight over the public service media has become a symbol of the defense of liberal democratic values and institutions," Eibl said.
As anger has swelled, the government has sought to calm the situation. Babis has said that a new proposal, which would see public media funding moved off budget and editorial independence guaranteed, would be drawn up and made available for a full and open debate.
However, critics remain unimpressed, noting a lack of any detail and the fact that other members of the government appear determined to remain on course.
Million Moments for Democracy has insisted the pressure must continue.
"Words are worth nothing," the group said. "While people stand up for independent media, the government continues to act as if it owns the country."
With little sign that the opposition will dissipate, the government faces a choice.
It has the parliamentary majority it needs to push the bill through and defeat any likely vetoes from the upper house Senate and President Petr Pavel .
Polls suggest political support for the government has been weakened and could diminish further if the protests expand to include growing frustrations over the cost of living and housing, as happened recently with student-led protests in France and other European countries .
"The real risk for the government is that the media issue becomes a lightning rod for broader dissatisfaction," said Martin Vokalek of the Prague-based EUROPEUM Institute for European Policy.
The PM announced that he will not attend the Velvet Revolution anniversary celebrations on November 17, which are hugely symbolic, in the hope that his absence might "calm the tense situation."
However, there's little concern that the Czech protests could descend into violence.
Analysts note that the anger in Czechia remains tightly focused on the public media proposal and continues to be expressed in a similar way to the seismic events of the country's modern history.
"I would not expect French-style scenes," Vokalek told DW, noting that the same "large, peaceful and civic Czech protest culture," which gave the Velvet Revolution and 1993's Velvet Divorce from Slovakia their name, is still strong.

A crushing local election result across the country has left South Africa's ruling ANC searching for answers. Experts say the vote reflects public frustration with service delivery failures — signaling a political shift.
South Africa's governing African National Congress (ANC) party is forced to confront its worst electoral setback to date after securing under 31% of the vote in the country's significant local government elections; party leaders themselves have described the result as "catastrophic."
This outcome marks a steep decline for the party that had once led South Africa's liberation struggle; the party that had dominated the country's political landscape since the end of apartheid in 1994.
The result reflects growing public frustration about the ANC's lack of performance in key areas such as skyrocketing unemployment, poor service delivery, local governance failures and years of graft and corruption — sometimes at the highest levels of government.
Tasnim Essop, a researcher at the Society, Work and Politics Institute (SWOP) at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, says it is time for the party to undertake some serious introspection. She believes that the ANC has to confront a long list of difficult questions about governance, leadership and accountability.
"You're talking about issues like water, electricity, housing, public services at the basic municipal level. And those kinds of things have been key issues. And ... research has shown that unemployment is also a big part of what drives people to vote in certain ways" she told DW.
Essop also highlights the fact that the outcome of the vote didn't happen overnight, and that it rather reflects a slow erosion of public confidence in the erstwhile ruling party over a long period.

DW correspondent Dianne Hawker-Kalubi, who reported from various polling stations during the election, agrees with that observation, stressing that many of the voters she had spoken to expressed "a lot of frustration, a lot of concern about basic services not being delivered" for years.
Mokhiri Phooko, a Cape Town resident, said that "people are losing hope" across the country after over three years of the political landscape being dominated by late President Nelson Mandela's party:
"You promised us jobs, why [are] you not keeping up the end of your bargain right," she told Reuters, stressing that "(t)he unemployment rate went up drastically" in the past few years.
The ANC itself meanwhile has acknowledged that things have to change: In a statement , the party announced that its National Executive Committee would convene a special meeting to deal with the "serious political responsibility to listen to the people, confront its shortcomings and provide leadership."
Furthermore, the party also has to prepare a framework for upcoming coalition negotiations at the same time — many times involving some of its biggest rivals, as was the case after the 2024 general elections .
The election results therefore signal a broader shift in South African politics, with voter support increasingly spread across multiple parties rather than being concentrated behind a single dominant force.
While nationally, the ANC remained the country's largest party, opposition parties made significant gains; the Democratic Alliance (DA) managed to strengthen its position across several major urban centers.
Meanwhile the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party, launched by former President Jacob Zuma in late 2023, performed rather strongly in the KwaZulu-Natal provice despite entering the political arena so recently.
At the local level, smaller civic organizations and community-based movements also recorded notable successes.
Essop describes this trend as a growing sense of "vote fluidity," with voters increasingly willing to move their support between parties instead of remaining loyal to a single political organization.
Some observers have already linked this drift to the idea of South Africans are moving beyond liberation-era loyalties; however, Essop opines: "I would be cautious to say that liberation politics are dead and gone," as many political parties continue to draw ther legitimacy and support from the country's liberation history — even if they no longer operate under the ANC banner.
Essop argues that the political shift does not signify a wholesale rejection of that liberation narrative itself, but rather a growing demand for effective governance and leadership.
For the ANC, the challenge now is rebuilding trust, with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa saying that the results are a challenge not just for his party but for all political parties to come together and perform better for citizens.
In a statement, Ramaphosa said that "[t]hose who have been elected to councils now need to prove themselves worthy of the trust placed in them by the South African people."
While the ANC still remains South Africa's largest political party, its latest setbacks at the polls underscore how much the country's political landscape is no longer what it was when apartheid ended.
The era of undisputed ANC loyalty and dominance appears to be over as voters are showing a greater willingness to support alternative parties and punish those they believe have fallen short.
Whether the ANC can reverse this decline will depend largely on how convincingly it can deliver not only improved public services, but effective change throughout.

Kenan Altınsaat, AA muhabirine, okullarda birinci dönem ara tatilinin öğrencilerce verimli ve faydalı geçirilebileceğini söyledi.
İnternetin hayatın önemli bir parçası haline geldiğine işaret eden Altınsaat, teknoloji devriminin içinde doğanların çocukluklarını dijital dünyada geçirdiğini dile getirdi.
Altınsaat, ekranlarla iç içe bulunan, internet üzerinden sosyalleşen, sokak oyunları yerine ekran oyunlarıyla eğlenen çocukların hayatı tamamen yeni ve farklı bir şekilde öğrendiğini anlattı.
Altınsaat, ebeveynlerin bu konularda daha sorumlu davranmasının önemine dikkati çekerek, şöyle devam etti:
"Ebeveynler, çocukların dijital ortamlarda güvenliğini ve gelişimini önemsemeli, onların 'faydalı, eğitici ve doğru' içeriklerle buluşmasına yardım etmelidir. Televizyon dahil bütün ekranlar ve internetle sağlıklı ve doğru ilişki kurabilmek için doğru dijital alışkanlıklar edinme konusunda çocuklara yol gösterilmeli, zaman sınırlamaları getirilerek internet kullanımında ölçülü olmaları sağlanmalıdır. Ebeveynler, 2026-2027 eğitim-öğretim yılının birinci dönem ara tatilinde çocuklarının internet kullanım alışkanlıklarını takip etmeli. Sağlıklı ve bilinçli internet kullanma alışkanlıkları, çocukların teknolojiden tamamen uzak durması anlamına gelmiyor. Teknoloji kullanımı konusunda gerçekçi ve net kurallar belirlemek, çocukların 'en fazla fayda ve en az zarar' ilkesi içinde kalmasını sağlar."
Tatilde çocukların daha yoğun şekilde dijital araçları kullanacağına dikkati çeken Altınsaat, "Aşırı dijital yüklenme, çocukların sosyal, fiziksel, duygusal ve zihinsel gelişimine zarar verebilir. Ekranların, internetin, dijital oyunların ve sosyal medyanın kuşatması altındaki çocuklar, teknoloji kullanımı konusunda ancak 'besleyici, doğru, yararlı, gerektiği kadar ve gerektiği zaman teknoloji' ilkesiyle sağlıklı alışkanlıklar geliştirebilir" dedi.
Altınsaat, çocukları sanal dünyada karşılaşacakları kötü niyetli kişilere, oyun görünümündeki tehlikeli akımlara ve zararlı içeriklere karşı korumanın iyi birer "dijital ebeveyn" olmanın en önemli yolu olduğunu ifade etti.
İnternet ve sosyal ağlarda çocukların video izleme, anlık mesajlaşma ve oyun oynama gibi çevrim içi alışkanlıklarının düzenli takip edilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Altınsaat, dijital platformlarda oynanan çevrim içi oyunlarda çocukların zihinsel, kültürel, sosyal gelişimlerini destekleyen eğitici oyunların tercih edilmesi gerektiğini kaydetti.
Altınsaat, dijital oyunların eğitim amaçlı kullanılmasıyla çocukların eğlenerek öğrenmesinin mümkün hale geldiğini dile getirerek, savaş, ölüm, şiddet, kavga, cinsellik ve İslamofobi ögeleri içeren dijital oyunlardan uzak durulmasının önem taşıdığını söyledi.
İnternette doğru bilgiye ulaşma yöntemini, "bilgiye farklı kaynaklardan ulaşmak, eleştirel bakış açısı geliştirmek ve bilgileri kıyaslamak" olarak aktaran Altınsaat, "İnternette karşılaşılan her bilgi doğru ve güvenilir değil." diye konuştu.
Altınsaat, internet ve sosyal medyadaki şüpheli linklere tıklanmaması, güvenilir olmayan mecralardan alışveriş yapılmaması, kişisel bilgilerin paylaşılmaması, bu ortamların gizlilik ve mahremiyet bilinciyle kullanılması gerektiğini dile getirdi.
Çocukların mahremiyet algısının zayıf olduğunu belirten Altınsaat, şunları kaydetti:
"Onların kolayca aldatılmalarının en önemli nedeni, internette hangi bilgileri paylaşacaklarını bilmemeleridir. Çocuklara, internet ve sosyal ağlarda tanımadıkları kişilerden uzak durması gerektiği söylenmelidir. Çocukların ekran başında geçirecekleri zaman sınırlandırılmalıdır. Hangi zaman dilimlerinde, ne kadar süre geçirecekleri net olarak belirlenmeli ve bu bir kural olarak uygulanmalıdır. Süreli kullanımın çok önemli olmasının yanı sıra internet ve sosyal medya ortamının çocuk tarafından 'doğru ve etik' kullanımının da çok önemli olduğu ebeveynler tarafından anlatılmalı, takip edilmelidir."
Altınsaat, teknolojinin amaç ve oyuncak olarak değil, araç olarak kullanılması gerektiğini ifade etti.
Çocukların, ekranın da etkisiyle daha hareketsiz bir yaşam sürdüğüne dikkati çeken Altınsaat, bu durumun yol açacağı olumsuzluklara karşı fiziksel aktivitelerin çoğaltılabileceğini söyledi.
Altınsaat, ebeveynlerin, "http://www.guvenlinet.org.tr" adresi ile Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı Bilgi Teknolojileri Genel Müdürlüğünce hazırlanan "Çocuklar Güvende Mobil Uygulaması" gibi mecralardan yararlanarak hem kendilerini hem de çocuklarını internetin zararlı içeriklerinden koruyabileceğini anlattı.
İnternette ve sosyal medyada karşılaşılan zararlı içeriklere dikkati çeken Altınsaat, bunların Bilgi Teknolojileri ve İletişim Kurumu bünyesindeki Bilgi İhbar Merkezine "https://www.ihbarweb.org.tr" adresinden iletilebileceğini sözlerine ekledi.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.
